content.headline: Form Follows Feeling
content.deck: On emotion as a structural material in visual communication
content.body: A talk on how designers translate mood into measurable decisions — scale, interval, contrast — and why the most rigorous systems often begin with an intuition that refuses to be named.

content.headline: Noise
content.deck: Signal, texture and the productive error
content.body: Printers, photocopiers and compression artefacts have quietly shaped two generations of graphic language. This evening looks at error as a design input rather than a defect.

content.headline: The Measured City
content.deck: Grids, plans and the politics of the right angle
content.body: From Cerdà's Barcelona to the modular tower block, the grid has promised order and delivered control. An architectural historian and a typographer compare notes.

content.headline: Notes on Silence
content.body: What is left out of a page is never empty. A close reading of posters, scores and book designs in which the unprinted area carries the argument.

content.headline: Type Is a Voice
content.body: A conversation with three type designers about drawing alphabets for languages, screens and institutions — and about the moment a typeface starts speaking for itself.

content.headline: Systems That Breathe
content.body: Visual identities are no longer single marks but sets of behaviours. How do you write rules that stay recognisable while producing thousands of different outcomes?

content.headline: Half Tone, Full Story
content.deck: A short history of the printed dot
content.body: The halftone screen made photographs printable and changed what newspapers, posters and record sleeves could say. A material history told through a single printing technique.

content.headline: After the Modernists
content.deck: What we kept, what we lost, what we should return
content.body: Swiss style was exported as neutrality. A critical look at the international typographic style, its blind spots, and the designers rewriting its rules today.

content.headline: Colour Without Permission
content.body: When does a colour combination stop being wrong and start being a style? Examples from protest graphics, club flyers and the overprint experiments of the 1960s.

content.headline: Reading Machines
content.deck: Design for readers that are not human
content.body: Barcodes, OCR fonts and today's vision models all read the page differently. What happens to graphic design when its audience includes software?

content.headline: Slow Posters
content.deck: Print in the age of the feed
content.body: A poster on a wall is seen for weeks, not seconds. A plea for images that reward a second look, and for the patience required to make them.

content.headline: The Shape of Things Not Yet Made
content.deck: Speculative design and the future as material
content.body: Prototypes, props and fictional objects let designers argue about futures before they arrive. An evening on design as a way of asking questions in public.
